h33-h33-2-b2-CONCcatblk10up10-20261024-c.hypothesis: At fixed count and mass, moving 10% of the dots out of the km-blocks with the least mapped-fault density into the blocks with the most re-concentrates the file onto the fault systems that the catalogue already proves are active in this crust.
h33-h33-2-b2-CONCcatblk10up10-20261024-c.mechanism: DTI pays for a relocated dot iff it lands within ~2.5 px of truth with kernel credit above ~0.05. h33-h33-2-b2-CONCcatblk10up10-20261024-c.non_fault_mimic: Catalogue density also tracks survey attention and bedrock exposure: well-mapped corridors may simply be where USGS and INGENIOUS looked, so the prior can concentrate mass onto already-exhausted ground and away from genuine new faults in unmapped basins.

h33-h33-2-b2-CONCENTRATIONphys10-2026102.hypothesis: Where magnetic horizontal gradient, isostatic-gravity slope and detrended-elevation slope are jointly high, the crust is more intensely broken per km^2, so truth density per km^2 is high there. This prior is built only from physics, so unlike the catalogue prior it cannot inherit mapping effort or exposure bias.
h33-h33-2-b2-CONCENTRATIONphys10-2026102.mechanism: Same fixed-S budget trade as catd10, with the block prior replaced by the 0.40 pct(tmi_hg) + 0.35 pct(iso_grav_anom_slope) + 0.25 pct(det_elev_slope) mix smoothed to 1 km. Differences ONLY which blocks are donors and receivers: same count, same mass, same spacing floor, same catalogue clearance.
h33-h33-2-b2-CONCENTRATIONphys10-2026102.non_fault_mimic: The same bands respond to non-tectonic contrasts: Tertiary volcanic flow margins, caldera ring fractures, pluton contacts, and lithologic scarps in resistant tuff. Because the physics mix is also what the H19-5 ridge mask was built to track, the implied redistribution is the mildest of the three variants.
h33-h33-2-b2-CONCENTRATIONphys10-2026102.falsifier: If phys10 and catd10 are both negative by >= 0.01 while their implied redistributions are near-disjoint, the axis itself (km-scale reallocation) is wrong, not just the prior.
